questions.q: The brachial plexus is formed primarily by the anterior rami of which spinal nerves?
questions.explain: The typical brachial plexus is formed by the anterior rami of C5, C6, C7, C8 and T1. Variations may produce prefixed or postfixed plexuses.
questions.alt: Schematic diagram of the brachial plexus showing roots, trunks, divisions, cords and terminal branches.
questions.credit: Image: Patrick John Duggan, public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.

questions.q: Which sequence correctly describes the organisation of the brachial plexus from proximal to distal?
questions.explain: The standard sequence is roots, trunks, divisions, cords and terminal branches. The cords are named in relation to the second part of the axillary artery.
questions.alt: Schematic diagram of the brachial plexus showing roots, trunks, divisions, cords and terminal branches.
